clue.text: With little room do heat somehow when terminally ill

indicators.note: somehow says these letters are arranged in some other way

parts.note: the letters of do heat, with a T the clue as held does not supply, rearranged
close means cramped, with little space to spare

explanation.surface: A stuffy, overheated sickroom for someone who is dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the fodder into TODEATH, but DO HEAT has only six letters; a T is missing, so the clue as printed is a letter short.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone close to death is nearly dying, the state of a patient whose illness is fatal and far advanced.

clue.text: Snootily ignore to perform an autopsy

explanation.surface: A haughty pathologist who will not acknowledge anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone dead is to snub them completely; taken literally, slicing into a corpse is what a pathologist does at a post-mortem.

clue.text: Ring railway to famous international airport

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Taking the train out to a well-known airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is just a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Orly is one of the main airports serving Paris, so it fits a famous international air terminal.

clue.text: Relaxation prohibited, so withdraw cautiously

parts.note: ease is rest or freedom from strain
out can mean ruled out or banned, as in 'smoking is out'

explanation.surface: With breaks banned, someone retreats carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease out is to remove or leave gently, a careful, gradual withdrawal.

clue.text: On and on about unruly sly sole male heir

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the two copies of the word on go round the rearranged letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: unruly means out of order, so the letters of sly are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone droning on and on about a wild, crafty boy who stands to inherit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the two copies of 'on' go round the letters that 'unruly' scrambles; 'and' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A family's one boy is its only male child and so the single son to inherit.

clue.text: Scratch out a living as an engraver?

definitions.text: Scratch out a living as an engraver?

parts.words: Scratch out a living as an engraver?
parts.note: scratching out a living normally means scraping by, but an engraver literally makes a living by scratching lines into metal

explanation.definitionFit: To engrave a plate is to cut lines into it with acid or a tool, exactly the scratching the clue describes.

clue.text: To the navy much trouble!

parts.note: taken as written
RN stands for the Royal Navy
ado is fuss or bother, as in Much Ado About Nothing

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a whirlwind of trouble has hit the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link word; the whole clue also serves as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating windstorm brings great trouble, especially to ships at sea; the Tornado was also an RAF warplane.

clue.text: What strong fencer once managed to do to prove untrustworthy

definitions.text: What strong fencer once managed to do

explanation.surface: A powerful swordsman turning out to be unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a loose pun: a strong fencer might break one's sWORD, the phrase with an extra S.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to keep a promise shows unreliability; a fencer strong enough to snap a blade could break one's sword, the phrase with an S added.

clue.text: Bed-time-story-lover's plea? I don't believe it!

explanation.surface: A child at bedtime begging for one more story.
explanation.definitionFit: A child keen on stories begs for one more; the same words are an idiom expressing disbelief at a tall tale.

clue.text: Disconcerts disconcerted starlet

indicators.note: disconcerted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of starlet are jumbled

explanation.surface: A flustered young actress unsettles people.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve or fluster someone is to put them off their stroke, a synonym of disconcert.

clue.text: Chlorophyll producer in Switzerland

explanation.surface: A green plant growing somewhere in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is a green fodder plant, also called alfalfa, that makes chlorophyll; it is also a Swiss city and lake.

clue.text: Lincoln died, but certainly not here

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln
D is the usual abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Abraham Lincoln's death, which did not happen in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone in bed is at home asleep, so certainly not here; Lincoln did in fact die in a bed, which adds a twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in bed means being away sleeping, so the person is not present at work or in company.

clue.text: Don't waste water

parts.note: the instruction not to waste something means put it to use
the instruction not to waste something means put it to use

explanation.surface: A conservation slogan urging people to save water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't waste' becomes 'do use', which run together gives the answer; 'water' looks like part of the slogan but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench something or put out a fire by throwing liquid on it is to wet it thoroughly.

clue.text: Computer language everyone can summon up

parts.note: C is a widely used programming language
all means every person

explanation.surface: A programming language anybody can bring up on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a link word joining wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon someone is to call them to appear.

clue.text: Dickensian spiv whose lips were never without a cigarette

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
something never absent from the lips is always in them

explanation.surface: A Dickens villain portrayed as a chain smoker.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG is everyday British slang for a cigarette; with one always 'in' his mouth he is FAG IN. Fagin is the thieves' master in Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Fagin is the crooked fence who runs a gang of boy pickpockets in Oliver Twist, a shady dealer of the spiv kind.

clue.text: I'd try tidying up if in this condition

definitions.text: I'd try tidying up if in this condition

indicators.note: tidying up means rearranging, so the letters of I'd try are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they would clean up if the place were grubby.
explanation.definitionFit: Grubby or soiled things are the ones that need cleaning, exactly why anyone would tidy up.

clue.text: Ancient mariner told Sal differently

indicators.note: differently says the letters of told Sal are set out in another order

explanation.surface: An old sailor spinning his yarn to a woman named Sal in his own way.
explanation.definitionFit: An experienced, weathered sailor is a sea dog, a seasoned seaman of long standing.

clue.text: Highly offensive racket in which retired doctor is caught

indicators.note: is caught says the doctor's letters are trapped inside the din

parts.note: a racket is a loud din or noise

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the letters for doctor are read backwards

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A loud row in which an elderly doctor gets trapped is deeply unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the doctor round, and 'in which ... is caught' says the din goes round him; 'Highly offensive' means foul, not rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Noxious, foul-smelling things are extremely unpleasant or disgusting.

clue.text: Suffer humiliation if wrongly attired

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of attired are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Being humiliated for turning up badly dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for having to accept insult or disgrace meekly, being forced to grovel.

clue.text: Put out at the road junction

explanation.surface: Stopping the engine at a road junction.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch off a light is to extinguish it; a side road branching from a main one is a junction you take.

clue.text: An idea nevertheless needing time initially

parts.note: though can mean however or nevertheless, as in 'it rained; we went, though'

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word time

explanation.surface: A concept that nonetheless requires a little time to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link word placing the T after THOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion formed in the mind is a product of thinking, the noun form.

clue.text: Understand the pistol cannot be fired

explanation.surface: Grasping that a gun is jammed and will not shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to cottoning on to it; a gun with its safety on cannot be fired.

clue.text: Cut a pastry dish for the conductor

parts.note: to clip is to cut or trim
a pie is a dish baked in pastry

explanation.surface: Slicing a pie for an orchestra leader.
explanation.walkthrough: A clippie was a British bus conductor, often a woman, who clipped tickets; the musical conductor reading is the false path.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for a woman who collected fares on a bus or tram.

clue.text: Case suggests none should be granted bail

definitions.text: suggests none should be granted bail

explanation.surface: A legal case in which no defendants are released.
explanation.definitionFit: A large soft bag carries everything; keep all prisoners locked up and nobody gets bail.

clue.text: Minor part of lock

explanation.surface: A young person fiddling with part of a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A child under a guardian's care is a ward; wards are also the ridges inside a lock that only the right key passes.

clue.text: Namely how one should move a caravan

definitions.text: how one should move a caravan

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to shift a holiday trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: That is to say, used to introduce specifics; a car pulls a caravan by hitching it behind, so you tow it.

clue.text: Black mark for a group of second-raters

parts.note: B is the grade below A, so second-rate
a lot is a group or batch, as at an auction

explanation.surface: Being labelled a bunch of inferiors is a stain on one's record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'of' are link words; B grade means second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain or blemish on a reputation is a mark of disgrace.

clue.text: Be about it and get your teeth stuck into it

definitions.text: get your teeth stuck into it

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Encouragement to tackle a task with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip with the teeth is to chomp, literally sinking them in.

clue.text: Upset keen prima donna

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: avid means eager or keen

explanation.surface: A temperamental opera star who is eager to be upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading female singer of an opera, or a temperamental star.

clue.text: Also going back into boxing arena cheering

indicators.note: into places the reversed letters inside the arena's word

parts.note: boxers fight in a ring

indicators.note: going back says the word for also is written backwards

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: Fans in a boxing hall shouting encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns TOO into OOT, which goes 'into' RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporting noisily, as fans do in American English when they root for a team.

clue.text: I'm going in to chatter to a high churchman

indicators.note: going in says the first letters are placed inside the word for chatter

parts.note: to prate is to chatter idly
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone about to go and gossip with an archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An archbishop of senior rank, such as the head of a national church, holds that title.

clue.text: When many a heart is broken fielding

definitions.text: When many a heart is broken

explanation.surface: Romantic heartbreak after a dance, or a cricketer chasing a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian song tells of hearts aching once the dance is over; a fielder in cricket chases the struck ball.
